question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2},\, & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X>Y).$
question.worked_solution:
If $f(x,y)$ is a joint probability density function for the random variables $X$ and $Y$ and $A⊂{R}^{2},$ then

$$
P((X,Y)\in A)={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

Notice that $f(x,y)$ is nonnegative in the region $D=[0,2]\times [0,1],$ and the event $A=\{X>Y\}$ corresponds to a subset of $D,$ shown as the shaded region below:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14215348/assets/2db85950b4d45901d79c173f264173d0c38046b2f087d0a28c8d5c69f024e31f.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>Y) & ={∬}_{A}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{A}\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\text{Area}(A) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
